extracted.intended_audience: national governments applying to or participating in OGP; OGP Support Unit staff and civil society stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Framework and procedures used by the Open Government Partnership to determine whether countries are eligible to join or remain in OGP, including four Core Eligibility metrics, a Values Check for new members, scoring rules, data sources, and Eligibility Review procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core Eligibility — overall pass threshold and point totals
rubrics_metrics.description: Core Eligibility is determined by evaluations of countries’ performance in four critical areas (Fiscal Transparency, Access to Information, Asset Disclosure, and Citizen Engagement). Countries can earn up to four points for their performance in each metric, for a total of 16 points. Some countries are only measured on three criteria (and can earn up to 12 points). If a country only has two or one criteria available, they are marked as 'Not enough data' in the Eligibility Score Sheet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To pass the Core Eligibility criteria, countries must earn at least 75% of the total possible points available to them (either 12 out of 16 or 9 out of 12). The scoring methodology for each metric is detailed in the metric-specific entries. Countries not assessed in any Core Eligibility metrics, or those with recent updates not yet reflected in the OGP Eligibility Database, are encouraged to provide additional information to the Support Unit for independent expert assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fiscal Transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: The timely publication of essential budget documents forms the basic building blocks of budget accountability and an open budget system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measurement: Two points awarded for the timely publication of each of two essential documents (Executive’s Budget Proposal and Audit Report) for open budgets, using a subset of indicators from the Open Budget Survey, conducted by the International Budget Partnership. Source: Open Budget Survey Document Availability Tracker.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to Information
rubrics_metrics.description: An access to information law that guarantees the public’s right to information and access to government data is essential to the spirit and practice of open government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measurement: 4 points awarded to countries with access to information laws in place, 3 points if a country has a constitutional provision guaranteeing access to information, and 1 point if a country has a draft access to information law under consideration. Countries with both a constitutional provision and a draft law under consideration will only be awarded the 3 points for the constitutional provision. Source: RTI Rating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Officials Asset Disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules that require public disclosure of income and assets for elected and senior public officials are essential to anti-corruption and open, accountable government. It is also important to make the data publicly available so citizens can monitor the disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measurement: 4 points awarded to countries with a law requiring officials to submit asset disclosures that also has any requirement that the information should be accessible to the public; 2 points awarded to countries with a law requiring officials to submit asset disclosures; 0 points for no law on asset disclosure. Source: Historically the World Bank’s Public Officials Financial Disclosure database (no longer available); the Support Unit is exploring alternative sources. If there are discrepancies identified, please contact [email protected].

rubrics_metrics.name: Citizen Engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Open Government requires openness to citizen participation and engagement in policy making and governance, including basic protections for civil liberties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measurement: Uses the Civil Liberties sub-indicator from the EIU Democracy Index (10 highest, 0 lowest). Scoring: 4 points for countries scoring above 7.5, 3 points for countries scoring above 5, 2 points for countries scoring above 2.5, and 0 points otherwise. Source: Latest available EIU Democracy Index.

rubrics_metrics.name: Values Check Assessment (for countries wishing to join OGP)
rubrics_metrics.description: An additional assessment implemented Sept 20, 2017 to ensure new countries joining OGP adhere to democratic governance norms and values in the Open Government Declaration. The Values Check applies only to countries that have yet to join OGP and does not affect existing OGP members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To pass the Values Check, countries must score three or higher (using ordinal scores) on at least one of the following two V-Dem indicators: (1) CSO Entry and Exit (extent of government control over entry/exit of civil society organizations) or (2) CSO Repression (extent government attempts to repress civil society organizations). Exceptional case: if V-Dem indicators are not collected for the country, the C&S Subcommittee will assess Values Check based on the CIVICUS Monitor; to pass using CIVICUS, a country must be rated 'Narrowed' or better at the time it submits its letter of intent to join OGP. For more information consult the latest V-Dem codebook.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling missing/updated data and submission of additional evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Countries not assessed in any of the Core Eligibility metrics, or those with recent updates not yet reflected in the OGP Eligibility Database, are encouraged to provide additional information to the Support Unit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any such information will be assessed independently by subject matter experts who will evaluate the submitted documents and evidence for participation to ensure that OGP participating countries remain in good standing and that performance measures are up to date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility Review process for countries failing to meet minimum criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: OGP member countries that fall below the minimum core eligibility for two consecutive years are automatically placed under 'Eligibility Review.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility Review may include enhanced support by the Support Unit and the Criteria and Standards Subcommittee to help the country meet minimum eligibility criteria; countries will remain under Eligibility Review until they meet the minimum eligibility score. The list of countries under review is published and updated regularly. Note: Eligibility Review alone will not lead to inactivity recommendations, but may inform a decision to recommend inactivity for countries also placed under Procedural Review. Policy approved by the SC on June 27, 2022 states countries below 75% should take immediate and explicit steps to meet the minimum by the next annual update (completed by the Support Unit in June each year).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data sources and caveats used in scoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Each metric relies on specified external data sources and indices to determine scores; not all sources cover all countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sources referenced: Open Budget Survey Document Availability Tracker (Fiscal Transparency), RTI Rating (Access to Information), World Bank’s Public Officials Financial Disclosure database (Asset Disclosure — historically; now unavailable), EIU Democracy Index (Citizen Engagement), V-Dem Dataset (Values Check), CIVICUS Monitor (Values Check fallback). The Support Unit is exploring alternative sources where original sources are no longer available. Missing metric coverage reduces the total possible points (e.g., three metrics → max 12). Countries with only two or one available metrics are marked 'Not enough data' in the Eligibility Score Sheet.
